title: Residual conormal injectivity at a regular affinoid point with separable residue field
statement:
Let $F$ be a field complete for a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value and let $r\geq0$. Put $T=F\langle x_1,\ldots,x_rangle$, the ring of series $\sum_{
u\in\mathbf N^r}a_
u x^
u$ for which, for every $\epsilon>0$, only finitely many coefficients have $|a_
u|\geq\epsilon$, with coefficientwise addition and Cauchy multiplication. Choose $s\geq0$ and $f_1,\ldots,f_s\in T$, put $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$ and $B=T/I$, and let $\mathfrak n\subset T$ be a maximal ideal containing $I$. Put $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak n/I\subset B$ and $\kappa=T/\mathfrak n=B/\mathfrak m$. Suppose $\kappa/F$ is a finite separable extension (each element has a minimal polynomial over $F$ with distinct roots), and the local ring $B_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Give $I/\mathfrak n I$ its quotient $\kappa$-vector-space structure. The rule taking $g\in I$ to its termwise derivatives modulo $\mathfrak n$ descends to an injective $\kappa$-linear map
$$I/\mathfrak n I\longrightarrow\kappa^{\oplus r},\qquad [g]\longmapsto igl(\partial g/\partial x_i mod\mathfrak n igr)_{i=1}^r.$$
Only regularity at the specified point is assumed; no regularity after coefficient-field extension is assumed. The cases $r=0$, $s=0$, and $I=0$ are included.

source.place: Conrad, Irreducible components of rigid spaces, proof of Lemma 3.3.1, printed p.510: regular point with separable residue extension is smooth; section 1.1, printed p.477: algebraic and analytic local rings have the same completion. Continuous conormal residue-fibre consequence from Temkin, Excellent_Desingularization.pdf, Proposition 3.3.2 proof, printed pp.20--21. Agent-formulated algebraic-localization version; both archival PDFs WANTED.

proof.text:
Write $D_i$ for the termwise derivative. Its coefficients are $(
u_i+1)a_{
u+e_i}$, and $|
u_i+1|\leq1$; hence it is again restricted. Comparing the finite sums for each coefficient gives $D_i(ab)=aD_i(b)+bD_i(a)$. For $a\in\mathfrak n$ and $g\in I\subseteq\mathfrak n$, this puts $D_i(ag)$ in $\mathfrak n$. Thus $D_i$ kills $\mathfrak nI$ after reduction, and $D_i(ag) mod\mathfrak n= ar a(D_i(g) mod\mathfrak n)$ for every $a\in T$, $g\in I$. This proves that the displayed map $d:I/\mathfrak nI	o\kappa^r$ exists and is $\kappa$-linear.

proof.text: Put $R=T_{\mathfrak n}$, $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak nR$ and $J=IR$. Apply [lem-per-tate-separable-local-cotangent-coordinates]: $R$ is regular local, $R/\mathfrak p=\kappa$, and $\theta:\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p^2\simeq\kappa^r$ has the stated derivative formula. Its hypotheses are exactly the completeness, nontrivial absolute value, maximality and finite separability assumed here. Since $I\subseteq\mathfrak n$, we have $J\subseteq\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient], $R/J\simeq B_{\mathfrak m}$, so $R/J$ is regular local by the hypothesis of the item.

proof.text:
The rule $\alpha:I/\mathfrak nI	o J/\mathfrak pJ$, $[g]\mapsto[g/1]$, is an isomorphism. Here is the fraction argument, using [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Every element of $J$ is $g/u$ with $g\in I$ and $u
otin\mathfrak n$ (combine the finitely many denominators). Choose $a\in T$ with $au\equiv1\pmod{\mathfrak n}$. Then $g/u-ag=(1-au)g/u\in\mathfrak pJ$, proving surjectivity. If $g/1\in\mathfrak pJ=(\mathfrak nI)R$, write $g/1=h/u$ with $h\in\mathfrak nI$, $u
otin\mathfrak n$. Equality of fractions supplies $v
otin\mathfrak n$ with $v(ug-h)=0$, so $vug\in\mathfrak nI$. Choose $b\in T$ with $bvu\equiv1\pmod{\mathfrak n}$. Then $g=bvug+(1-bvu)g\in\mathfrak nI$. Thus $\alpha$ is injective as well. All maps respect $\kappa$-scalars via the residue map.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-independent-generators] to $R$ and $J$. Both $R$ and $R/J$ are regular local by Step 2, and $J\subseteq\mathfrak p$. It gives generators $u_1,\ldots,u_c$ of $J$ whose classes in $\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p^2$ are linearly independent over $\kappa$.

source.place: Tag 00NR, lemma-regular-quotient-regular; Tag 00CT, proposition-localize-quotient; explicit residual-fraction and linear-combination arguments supplied by the agent.

proof.text: Inclusion induces $\beta:J/\mathfrak pJ\to\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p^2$, since $\mathfrak pJ\subseteq\mathfrak p^2$. If $z=\sum_jb_ju_j\in J$ maps to zero, then $\sum_j\bar b_j[u_j]=0$. The independence from Step 4 forces all $\bar b_j=0$, hence $b_j\in\mathfrak p$ and $z\in\mathfrak pJ$. Thus $\beta$ is injective. This includes $c=0$.

source.place: Tag 00NR, lemma-regular-quotient-regular; Tag 00CT, proposition-localize-quotient; explicit residual-fraction and linear-combination arguments supplied by the agent.

proof.text: For $g\in I$, the coordinate formula in [lem-per-tate-separable-local-cotangent-coordinates] gives $(\theta\beta\alpha)([g])=(\overline{D_i g})_i=d([g])$. Therefore $d$ is the composite of an isomorphism, an injective map and an isomorphism, and is injective. When $r=0$, $T=F$ and the only maximal ideal is $0$, so $I=0$. When $s=0$ or $I=0$ the source vector space is zero. No scalar extension of $B$ has been used.
